outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles, restricts, or moves a bound on whether Con(ZFC + strongly compact) implies Con(ZFC + supercompact); the question remains open as stated. The in-window events found are neighbouring work (identity crises, lambda-strong compactness, a determinacy result for UA, measure-count and Prikry-forcing papers, two unrefereed Zenodo records on PFA and Ultimate-L, a ZF choiceless variant), and none of them addresses the equiconsistency question.
problem_asks: (1) The hypothesis: Con(ZFC + there is a strongly compact cardinal). (2) The conclusion: Con(ZFC + there is a supercompact cardinal). (3) The asserted link between them: that (1) implies (2), read as a consistency implication (a relative-consistency argument), not as a ZFC theorem deriving the existence of a supercompact from a strongly compact. Together with the converse, this is equiconsistency. The converse is not asked and is immediate in ZFC, since every supercompact cardinal is strongly compact. The statement names no specific cardinal and no background theory beyond ZFC.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'Strong Compactness and the Ultrapower Axiom' (arXiv:1710.03586), a short announcement of consequences of an abstract comparison principle, the Ultrapower Axiom (UA). The arXiv abstract reads 'We announce some consequences of an abstract comparison principle.' Search summaries of the PDF report that under UA the least strongly compact cardinal is supercompact, and that the paper poses as 'Question 1' whether UA is consistent with a supercompact cardinal, adding that the answer is probably yes. The PDF was not readable through WebFetch, so these details come from search summaries only.
events.revisions: v1 only (10 Oct 2017), per the arXiv abstract page; no later version listed.
events.delivers: Under UA, a hypothesis and not a ZFC theorem, the least strongly compact cardinal is supercompact. Restricted to the least strongly compact cardinal and conditional on UA. Establishes no ZFC consistency implication.
events.remains: The unconditional implication Con(ZFC + strongly compact) to Con(ZFC + supercompact). Also whether UA is consistent with a supercompact cardinal (the announcement's own Question 1). Other strongly compact cardinals are not addressed.
events.doubts: An announcement with a one-sentence arXiv abstract; the body was not read directly, so theorem numbering and wording come from search summaries. The result is conditional on UA, whose consistency with a supercompact cardinal is itself open by the author's own statement.
events.direction: Supports equality of strong compactness and supercompactness for the least strongly compact cardinal, under UA. Cuts toward a 'yes' answer to the equiconsistency question only conditionally.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'The Ultrapower Axiom and the equivalence between strong compactness and supercompactness' (arXiv:1810.05058), version 1 submitted 9 October 2018; no later version listed on arXiv. Quoted from the fetched arXiv abstract page: 'we prove that the notions are equivalent except for a class of counterexamples identified by Menas'; and 'This is evidence that strongly compact and supercompact cardinals are equiconsistent.' A search summary identifies 'Strong compactness and the ultrapower axiom I: the least strongly compact cardinal' (J. Math. Logic, 2022) as the published form of this preprint. That identification is not confirmed, because the NSF PAR copy was unreadable through WebFetch.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (9 Oct 2018). Journal publication reported as 2022 (J. Math. Logic), identity with this preprint unconfirmed.
events.delivers: Under UA, strong compactness and supercompactness coincide up to Menas's counterexamples (per the abstract; the search summary of the slides adds that a cardinal is strongly compact iff it is supercompact or a measurable limit of supercompacts). Conditional on UA. The author describes the equiconsistency consequence as evidence, not proof.
events.remains: The unconditional ZFC implication. The consistency of UA with a supercompact cardinal. The analysis of the second strongly compact cardinal, which the author defers to a sequel (per the 2022 abstract as summarised).

checked_by.who: Journal of Mathematical Logic, as publisher of 'Strong compactness and the ultrapower axiom I' (2022), if that is the published form of this preprint
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, per a search summary; the acceptance of this exact preprint is not independently confirmed

events.doubts: The equivalence is conditional on UA, and UA's consistency with supercompact cardinals is the open question itself, so the conditional result cannot be read off as progress on the unconditional problem. The identity of the 2018 preprint with the 2022 JML paper is unverified.
events.direction: Conditional support for equiconsistency (the 'yes' direction). Gives no unconditional implication.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'The Ultrapower Axiom': Harvard PhD dissertation (dated 2019 on Harvard DASH; the filename reads GOLDBERG-DISSERTATION-2019), posted to arXiv as 2006.03293 on 5 June 2020 (281 pages). Later published as a De Gruyter book (2022, per the author's homepage). Quoted from the fetched arXiv abstract page: 'The problem is closely related to the more precise question of the equiconsistency of strongly compact cardinals and supercompact cardinals.' and 'Moreover, we establish that under the Ultrapower Axiom, strong compactness and supercompactness are essentially equivalent.'
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (5 Jun 2020). The 2019 date is the dissertation's DASH filename, not opened; the book is 2022 per the author's homepage.
events.delivers: Under UA, and under the standing hypothesis that a supercompact cardinal exists, strong compactness and supercompactness are essentially equivalent. The thesis presents this as evidence that the inner model problem for supercompacts can be solved. Conditional on UA and on a supercompact cardinal.
events.remains: The unconditional implication, which the thesis's own framing ties to the inner model problem for supercompact cardinals. The consistency of UA with a supercompact cardinal.
events.doubts: The equivalence rests on two hypotheses the question does not grant: UA, and a supercompact cardinal. The thesis itself describes the inner model problem for supercompacts as one of the central open problems in set theory. Only the abstract page was read.
events.direction: Conditional support for equiconsistency; the unconditional direction is left to the inner model problem.

events.what_happened: Alejandro Poveda, 'Axiom A and supercompactness' (arXiv:2406.12776, math.LO), version 1 submitted 18 June 2024. Per the abstract page: produces a model where every supercompact cardinal is C^(1)-supercompact with inaccessible targets; introduces Axiom A, shown compatible with Woodin's I0 cardinals; answers a question of Gitman and Goldberg on supercompactness and cardinal-preserving extendibility; and incidentally suggests supercompactness is the strongest large cardinal notion preserved by Radin forcing. The table of contents lists a section 'Axiom A and the Ultimate-L conjecture'; the body was not read.
events.revisions: v1 only (18 Jun 2024), per the abstract page.
events.delivers: Consistency results about the structure of supercompact cardinals (identity-crisis configurations: C(1)-supercompactness with inaccessible targets, under Axiom A). It does not involve strongly compact cardinals and establishes nothing about their equiconsistency with supercompacts.
events.direction: No direction on the question. It concerns supercompacts among themselves and does not cut for or against equiconsistency.
events.object: A forcing model in which every supercompact cardinal is C^(1)-supercompact with inaccessible targets, built from the new Axiom A. Described in the abstract only; not a counterexample to anything the question asserts.

events.what_happened: Assaf Rinot, Zhixing You, Jiachen Yuan, 'Ketonen's question and other cardinal sins' (arXiv:2408.01547). Version 1 submitted 2 August 2024; version 2 revised 27 November 2025. Per the fetched abstract page: answers Ketonen's question by showing a weakly compact cardinal carrying an indecomposable ultrafilter need not be measurable; and solves 'a problem by Bagaria and Magidor concerning strong compactness' and a Lambie-Hanson–Rinot question on the C-sequence number. A search summary states the Bagaria–Magidor part as: for proper-class-many lambda, the least lambda-strongly compact cardinal is singular. The body was not read.
events.revisions: v1 2 Aug 2024; v2 27 Nov 2025 (per fetched abstract page). No journal publication found.
events.delivers: Per the abstract as summarised: for proper-class-many lambda, the least lambda-strongly compact cardinal is singular; and a weakly compact with an indecomposable ultrafilter need not be measurable. The page does not mention supercompact cardinals, so the paper contains nothing on the supercompact side of the question.
events.direction: Neutral to the question. It concerns lambda-strong compactness and singularity, not the comparison of strongly compact with supercompact cardinals in consistency strength.

events.what_happened: Sean Cox, 'Vopenka's Principle, Maximum Deconstructibility, and singly-generated torsion classes' (arXiv:2412.19380, math.LO). Version 1 submitted 26 Dec 2024; version 2 on 8 Jan 2025; version 3 on 21 May 2025. Per the fetched abstract page: proves that MD is equivalent to Vopenka's Principle. The abstract notes that MD was known to follow from Vopenka's Principle and to imply an omega-1-strongly compact cardinal. Nothing about supercompact cardinals or equiconsistency.
events.revisions: v1 26 Dec 2024; v2 8 Jan 2025; v3 21 May 2025 ('title change and minor edits').
events.delivers: Equivalence of MD and Vopenka's Principle. It touches strongly compact cardinals only through the known implication VP to MD to omega-1-strong compactness. It does not compare the consistency strength of strongly compact and supercompact cardinals.

events.what_happened: Douglas Blue, Paul B. Larson, Grigor Sargsyan, 'Nairian Models' (arXiv:2501.18958, math.LO), single version submitted 31 January 2025. Per the fetched abstract page: introduces a hierarchy of models of the Axiom of Determinacy called Nairian models; builds a Nairian model of ZF in which omega-1 is supercompact; and, as a corollary, gives a negative answer to a question of Trang on whether ZF plus 'omega-1 is supercompact' is equiconsistent with ZFC plus a proper class of Woodin cardinals that are limits of Woodin cardinals.
events.delivers: In a choiceless setting (ZF with AD-type hypotheses), a model where omega-1 is supercompact, and a negative equiconsistency answer for a Woodin-limit hypothesis. It does not involve strongly compact cardinals, and it is not a ZFC result.
events.remains: The ZFC question on strongly compact versus supercompact cardinals, entirely.
events.direction: No bearing on the question. It is a different theory (ZF with AD-type models) and a different large cardinal hypothesis (omega-1 supercompact), though it shares the word 'supercompact' and an equiconsistency framing.

events.what_happened: Will Boney and Jonathan Osinski, 'Model-theoretic characterizations of large cardinals (Re)^2 visited' (arXiv, math.LO), submitted 21 May 2025; the abstract page lists a later revision dated 23 June 2026. Per the fetched abstract page: characterizes Pi_n-strong cardinals, Ord is Woodin, weak Vopenka's Principle and huge cardinals by compactness properties of logics; states that the compactness number of the Hartig quantifier logic L(I) can consistently exceed the first supercompact cardinal; and gives upward Lowenheim–Skolem numbers in terms of the first extendible cardinal.
events.revisions: v1 21 May 2025; a revision listed on 23 June 2026 (per the abstract page; content of the revision not read).
events.delivers: Logic-compactness characterizations of several large cardinals; a consistency result about the compactness number of L(I) relative to a supercompact. It makes no equiconsistency or consistency-strength comparison between strongly compact and supercompact cardinals.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Goldberg, 'The Ultrapower Axiom from Determinacy', listed on the author's homepage under Papers and Preprints; no arXiv identifier found. Per search summaries of the PDF, its Theorem 4.13 states that ZF + AD+ implies UA holds below Theta, using a coding theorem for measures (Kechris) and a generic ultrapower construction (Woodin). A search summary dates the PDF 31 October 2025; the homepage gives no date. Talk slides from February 2025 (per summaries) describe the joint result with Steve Jackson as AD implies UA below aleph-omega. The PDF was not readable through WebFetch, so these details are from summaries.
events.revisions: Homepage gives no date. Search summaries disagree on authorship: one describes it as sole-authored, another as joint with Jackson for the earlier aleph-omega version.
events.delivers: UA holds in a determinacy model of ZF + AD+ below Theta. This is a model of UA with no large cardinals in the ZFC sense. It produces no supercompact cardinal and no consistency implication from strong compactness.
events.remains: The question as stated is untouched. Goldberg's own open question, whether UA is consistent with a supercompact cardinal, is not addressed by this result as summarised.
events.doubts: The PDF was not read, and the Theta statement and the Jackson attribution come from summaries that disagree.
events.direction: No direction on the question. It shows UA can hold in a determinacy setting, which concerns the axiom's consistency with determinacy rather than with a supercompact.
people: Steve Jackson (co-author of the earlier aleph-omega result, per talk summaries)

events.what_happened: 'Zen Revista' and 'MFC', 'Inner Model Theory for Supercompact Cardinals and the Consistency of the Proper Forcing Axiom', Zenodo record 18109660 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18109660), published 31 December 2025, version 1, CC BY 4.0. Per the fetched record: claims to construct a canonical inner model L[E] for a supercompact cardinal, extending the hyper-Woodin hierarchy; claims that PFA gives a forcing extension if a supercompact exists in the core model K, and conversely; and concludes that ZFC plus a supercompact and ZFC plus PFA are equiconsistent. The record lists no affiliations.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the fetched record.
events.delivers: Per its abstract as summarised: a canonical model for a supercompact cardinal, and an equiconsistency of ZFC + supercompact with ZFC + PFA. It makes no claim about strongly compact cardinals, so it does not address the question's hypothesis.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, since the record says nothing about strongly compact cardinals.
events.doubts: An unrefereed Zenodo deposit. Authors appear only as 'Zen Revista' and 'MFC' with no listed affiliation on the record, and no expert discussion was found. The claims (a canonical inner model for a supercompact; PFA equiconsistency) would be major results, and none of the sources read discusses them.
events.direction: Concerns the inner model program for supercompacts, which the field names as the expected route to the question. It makes no claim about strongly compact cardinals, so on the question as stated it cuts neither way.
events.object: A claimed canonical inner model L[E] for a supercompact cardinal, given in the abstract only; not checkable from the sources read.

events.what_happened: 'Zen Revista' and 'MFC', 'The Ultimate L Conjecture and Inner Models for Supercompact Cardinals', Zenodo record 18485224 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18485224), published 4 February 2026, version 1, typed as a journal article. Per the fetched record: examines Woodin's Ultimate-L conjecture (a weak extender model for a supercompact satisfying V = Ultimate-L); claims structural consequences including the HOD Dichotomy, a universality theorem for weak extender models, the resolution of CH, and a shift from pure to strategic extender models.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the fetched record.
events.delivers: Per its abstract as summarised: consequences of the Ultimate-L conjecture. It makes no claim about strongly compact cardinals and no claim about equiconsistency.
events.doubts: An unrefereed deposit by the same unverified author group as the December 2025 record. The CH consequence it lists is already associated in the Ultimate-L literature with the axiom V = Ultimate-L, so the record adds no checked result on this question. No expert engagement was found.

events.what_happened: Arthur W. Apter, Eyal Kaplan, Alejandro Poveda, 'The number of measures on very large measurable cardinals' (arXiv:2603.11710), version 1 submitted 12 March 2026. Per the fetched abstract page: studies how many normal measures a measurable cardinal can carry where inner-model methods are unavailable; states that the theorems exploit consequences of the Ultrapower Axiom; combines the Kimchi–Magidor result that the first n measurables can be strongly compact with prescribed measure counts; gives results for the first measurable above a supercompact and the first measurable limit of supercompacts; and strengthens an unpublished Goldberg–Woodin theorem and a Goldberg–Osinski–Poveda theorem.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the abstract page.
events.delivers: Measure-count results for measurable cardinals, under UA consequences. It makes no equiconsistency or consistency-strength statement about strongly compact versus supercompact cardinals.
events.doubts: The theorems use consequences of UA, which is not known to be consistent with a supercompact cardinal. Results are therefore conditional on that axiom's consequences, which is a limit on how the paper bears on the question.

events.what_happened: Tom Benhamou, Sebastiano Thei, Ben-Zion Weltsch, 'On the Intermediate Models of Strongly Compact Prikry Forcing' (arXiv:2605.09161), version 1 submitted 9 May 2026; version 2 revised 3 June 2026 (current). Per the fetched abstract page: characterizes the projections of strongly compact Prikry forcing through a combinatorial property using kappa-complete fine measures for a supercompact kappa; gives Rudin–Keisler-style criteria; and treats forcings of cardinality lambda.
events.revisions: v1 9 May 2026; v2 3 June 2026 (per the abstract page).
events.delivers: A characterization of projections between Prikry-type forcings. It makes no consistency-strength statement comparing strongly compact and supercompact cardinals.

events.what_happened: Edgar Valenzuela, 'Compactness via Consistency Properties' (arXiv:2609.26509), version 1 submitted 22 September 2026; version 2 on 23 September 2026 (current). Per the fetched abstract page: uses consistency properties to characterize strongly compact cardinals, with an adequate Model Existence Theorem for larger fragments.
events.revisions: v1 22 Sep 2026; v2 23 Sep 2026 (per the abstract page).
events.delivers: A characterization of strongly compact cardinals by consistency properties. It says nothing about supercompact cardinals or their consistency strength.
events.direction: No direction on the question. It concerns the characterization of strongly compact cardinals, not their comparison with supercompacts.

summary: The question is open as stated, and I found no in-window result that changes that. The status is set by three things: the Wikipedia article 'Strongly compact cardinal' (fetched; last edited 3 November 2024) says some set theorists conjecture the equiconsistency and that a proof is unlikely until a canonical inner model theory for supercompact cardinals exists; Goldberg's own 2017–2022 statements (arXiv:1710.03586, arXiv:1810.05058, arXiv:2006.03293, which the author describes as 'evidence' under UA and frames as open, with UA's consistency with a supercompact posed as Question 1); and the absence of any 2024–2026 paper that treats the question. The closest pre-window evidence is Goldberg's UA-conditional equivalence, which is the strongest body of work on the question but is conditional and pre-dates the window. The in-window events are all neighbouring: Poveda (identity crises among supercompacts, June 2024); Rinot–You–Yuan (lambda-strong compactness and Ketonen's question, August 2024, v2 November 2025); Cox (Vopenka's Principle and maximum deconstructibility, December 2024); Blue–Larson–Sargsyan (a choiceless ZF model with omega-1 supercompact, January 2025); Boney–Osinski (logic characterizations, May 2025); Goldberg's UA-from-determinacy PDF (2025, not read directly); Apter–Kaplan–Poveda (measure counts under UA, March 2026); Benhamou–Thei–Weltsch (projections of strongly compact Prikry forcing, May 2026); Valenzuela (characterization of strongly compact by consistency properties, September 2026); and two unrefereed Zenodo deposits by 'Zen Revista' and 'MFC' (December 2025 on PFA and an inner model for a supercompact; February 2026 on the Ultimate-L conjecture). The Zenodo records are the only in-window items that touch the inner-model route the field names as the prerequisite, and that is the close call. Read on the question as stated, they make no claim about strongly compact cardinals and no equiconsistency claim between strongly compact and supercompact cardinals, and their authorship and refereeing cannot be verified from the record. I judge them not to move the question. Close calls: (a) the Blue–Larson–Sargsyan paper states an equiconsistency-type result, but for ZF with AD-type hypotheses and omega-1 supercompact, so it is a different question; (b) the Goldberg UA-from-determinacy result proves UA in a determinacy model, which is a UA-consistency result, not a supercompact one. AI search: I searched for AI involvement in this problem through the named topic, lab announcements, news and the OpenAI release of 6 October 2026. None names a system for this problem, so ai.none_found is true on every event. The OpenAI openai/math release (722 manuscripts per news, 719 per its README, from an unreleased internal model) was checked for relevance: I read its CONTENTS.md across the full 636,312 characters in summarised chunks and found no manuscript mentioning strongly compact, supercompact, large cardinal or Ultrapower terms; its set-theory items (240 on Shelah's categoricity, 244 on the Partition Principle not implying Choice, 323 on a separable quotient problem independent relative to a measurable) are about other questions. The Partition Principle claim is contested by Karagila per a news report and is not this problem. An August 2026 news item says an unreleased Claude model was involved in progress on a major open problem, unnamed and unverified, and nothing links it to this question; I have not credited any Claude model here. Lean/Mathlib: I found no formalization of large cardinals or supercompact cardinals, so machine_checked is null throughout. Prior record: an existing deep-dive record for this key (data/mark_2026-09-22/deepdive/out) reaches the same open status; I re-derived the status from the sources rather than relying on it.
competing_reading: The strongest case for counting something as progress is that Goldberg's UA-based equivalence (2018, with the 2022 journal publication and the 2020 book/thesis) is the most substantive treatment of the question, still cited, and that its conditional equivalence could be read as a restricted case that already gives equiconsistency under a hypothesis believed consistent. That reading would still not move any in-window event, because all of it pre-dates 26 January 2024. The in-window route for that reading is the Zenodo inner-model claims: a reader who accepted the December 2025 canonical inner model for a supercompact as a theorem could argue it supplies the inner-model ingredient the field calls the expected route, and so counts as partial progress. I think that is weak: the record does not mention strongly compact cardinals, has no reviewer or named expert, and the sources I read do not treat its claims as established.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A proof, in ZFC or relative to a stated large cardinal theory, that the consistency of a strongly compact cardinal yields the consistency of a supercompact, or a counterexample to the implication. (b) A canonical inner model for a supercompact cardinal accepted by named experts, since that is the route the literature names; the December 2025 record would count only after expert verification and only if it addressed strongly compact cardinals. (c) Goldberg's promised sequel to 'Strong compactness and the ultrapower axiom I', which the 2022 abstract says will give the complete analysis of strong compactness and supercompactness under UA; a conditional result would not settle the question but would show whether the UA route moves. (d) A confirmed answer to whether UA is consistent with a supercompact cardinal (Goldberg's Question 1), which would remove the conditionality of the 2018 equivalence.
